articles.title: How I think engineers grow when AI writes the first draft
articles.excerpt: For most of my career an engineer learned the craft by doing the small things first. Fix the typo in the error message, then the off-by-one, then the feature behind a flag, and somewhere in the second…
articles.body: For most of my career an engineer learned the craft by doing the small things first. Fix the typo in the error message, then the off-by-one, then the feature behind a flag, and somewhere in the second year the design of a whole module. AI coding tools now write a decent first draft of most of those small things, and I think that quietly removes the ladder a lot of us climbed. I do not think the answer is to keep people away from the tools. It is to be deliberate about where the learning now happens. What the small tasks were teaching The typo fix was never about the typo. It taught how the code is organized, how a change gets reviewed, what the tests look like, and how it feels to ship. When a tool does the typing, the person still needs those lessons, and they are no longer free.

articles.title: The Taurid meteor shower peaks tonight — and fireballs could steal the show
articles.excerpt: The Taurid meteor shower could spawn dazzling fireballs in the coming weeks! Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: Heads up stargazers! The Taurid meteor shower is upon us, bringing multiple peaks of activity that could see spectacular shooting stars and fireballs brighten November's sky. Here's where and when to look. What is the Taurid meteor shower(s)? Every autumn, Earth plows through streams of debris left behind by Comet Encke, a 3-mile-wide (4.8-kilometer) ice body that orbits the sun once every 3.3 years. These debris streams produce two branches of the Taurid meteor shower : The Southern Taurids, active from Sept. 20 to Nov. 20 and the Northern Taurids, active from Oct. 20 to Dec. 10. As Earth plows through the debris streams, tiny particles slam into our atmosphere at 65,000 miles per hour (104,607 kilometers per hour), producing dazzling streaks of light across the night sky.
